headline: What Should I Do If I'm Accused of a Hit and Run?

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
Finding yourself accused of a hit and run can be a truly terrifying experience, bringing with it a lot of fear and uncertainty about what comes next. It's totally natural to feel stressed, but knowing the right steps to take immediately can make a huge difference in the outcome. Don't panic; instead, focus on protecting your rights.

First and foremost, don't talk to law enforcement without legal counsel. Anything you say can and will be used against you, even if you think you're just explaining your side. Politely decline to answer questions until you've spoken with an attorney. This is your right and an important protection.

Next, resist the urge to contact the other party or return to the scene. While your intentions might be good, this could complicate your case or even be interpreted negatively. Let your legal team handle all communications and investigations.

Then, start gathering any information you have about the incident. This could include the date, time, location, a description of the other vehicle, and any reasons why you might have left the scene (even if you weren't aware of the accident at the time). This information will be vital for your defense.

Finally, and most importantly, seek legal representation immediately. A hit and run charge in California carries significant penalties, including potential jail time, hefty fines, and points on your driving record. An experienced attorney, like Angelo Reyes, can review the evidence, challenge the allegations, and work towards minimizing the impact on your life. Facing a hit and run charge is serious; secure professional legal assistance as soon as possible.
